memory_candidates.content: When a plan's Phase 4 verification bullet says a script 'exits 0' but the script also runs unrelated cross-cutting checks (e.g. check-extension-docs.sh's deployed-vs-source drift check), a source-store-only task that intentionally never redeploys to .claude/** will trip that unrelated check every time it touches a deployed script's source. This is not a defect to fix (redeploying would violate the source-store/deploy boundary) -- it is the correct trigger for closing that phase as [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] with a Reasoned Exclusions record naming the specific unrelated finding and grep-confirming zero occurrences of the actually-required check names (e.g. 'Rule R'/'Rule T').

For a Scope Hypothesis that says 're-measure X before trusting the recorded count, another concurrent task may have landed first,' the concrete safe pattern is: run the measurement command immediately before the mutating edit in the same tool-call batch as the edit itself, and record both the measured baseline and the post-edit count explicitly in the phase's verification output rather than trusting either the plan's recorded number or an assumption of concurrency-safety.
